notes: Apply sender-controller-diagnostic.patch, sender-loss-scan-diagnostic.patch, sender-loss-summary-diagnostic.patch and sender-open-diagnostic.patch to13cdebd. Both startup-clock and packet-round evidence corrections are absent to match the earlier diagnostic.

Only group0 is instrumented; this workload has one group. Six cached categories partition stable intervals between public Owner mutations; open_owner_ns measures actual Open time inside those mutations, including diagnostic request scans. No request is not an application-idle proof.

Waiting time splits at pacing eligibility and request expiry. Readiness is cached after each bounded mutation, not sampled from future state. A ready category can include owner/output-budget delay and exceptional probe-allowance exhaustion.
Load-only summaries use before/sent worker0 monitor snapshots. Their seven Open categories reconcile to about99.8% of the existing Open timer; clock-observation skew remains.

Grant eligible lateness is issued_at-max(prior_pacer_deadline,request_arrival), including window/epoch/host delay, not a timer-only metric. Grant budgets include subsequently unused bytes; successful physical bytes exclude them.
Fixed loss-scan counters add no allocations or syscalls; existing controller diagnostics add clock reads and immediate/1Hz monitor snapshots. No builds/tests overlap load.
Directions L->R/R->L; endpoint arrays L/R. Receiver sample goodput excludes drain; missing ratios include drain. 100% CPU is one CPU.
TAP SKBs, queue drops and expired frames use different units and cannot be added into an exact frame-loss total.
The summary greatly reduces empty scanning and continuations, but goodput remains far below either performance gate.
